text:
sam: Picking this up from Zendesk — customer (AcmeCorp) says their console usage charts are ~6 hours behind. report: https://acme.zendesk/01234 — says last data point at 00:00 UTC but live requests show 06:00 UTC.
elaine: Ugh, saw a support surge earlier. Any errors in ingestion? cc @jordan
jordan: I just checked the consumer group for hourly-rollups, offsets look stalled. kafka consumer lag ~11M messages on topic tenant-usage-hourly-partitions. Might be a consumer restart around 02:15 UTC.
sam: Do we have an alert fired? I don't see an incident in PagerDuty.
elaine: No P1, only a few alerts for consumer lag but they cleared. Could be that offsets rewound and reprocessed older messages slowly.
ingrid: Posting quick queries I ran:
```
-- last 3 hourly_rollup rows for tenant
SELECT ts, processed_at FROM hourly_rollups
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 3;
-- consumer lag
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group hourly-rollups
```
Results: last processed ts = 2024-11-18T00:00:00Z, consumer lag = 11,234,567
jordan: Logs show consumer crashed from OOM at 02:12 UTC, restarted by k8s at 02:14. After restart, it fell behind due to large backlog and batching backpressure. There's also ~3h of messages that need KV-refresh because of schema change.
elaine: Schema change? Which one?
jordan: Small schema tweak for embedding metadata merged yesterday — consumer has a compatibility path but it's slower because we run transformation step that calls a microservice for enrichment.
sam: Customer is asking for ETA. Can we do a targeted backfill for Acme only instead of full reprocess?
ingrid: Yes, we have a tenant-scoped backfill job. Steps I recommend:
1) Stop consumer for hourly-rollups for tenant routing (scale replica=0 for dedicated pod)
2) Run backfill with SQL filter tenant_id='acme' and time window 02:00-08:00 UTC
3) Monitor writes to hourly_rollups and console ingestion metrics
Command example:
```
./jobs/run-backfill --tenant acme --from 2024-11-18T02:00:00Z --to 2024-11-18T08:00:00Z --batch-size 10k
```
jordan: I'll own running the backfill. ETA ~ 45-60m to kick off and then the job will take ~30-90m depending on enrichment latencies.
sam: Please add an interim note to the Zendesk ticket so customer knows we're on it.
jordan: Added a note to ticket 01234: "We identified a consumer OOM and are running a tenant-scoped backfill; expected catch-up within ~2 hours."
elaine: After backfill we should consider making enrichment async to avoid blocking consumer throughput. Filing a follow-up with eng-runtime.
sam: Thanks. @etl-bot can you add a daily alert for consumer lag > 1M for >15m to avoid silent regressions?
etl-bot: alert created: trigger kafka.hourly_rollups.lag >1e6 for 15m, notify #eng-oncall and #support
ingrid: I'll watch console graphs and post when Acme's chart shows recent data.
jordan: Backfill started at 1729460500 (UTC). monitoring: write rate increasing, writes to hourly_rollups for tenant acme now showing recent timestamps.
sam: Great — keep updates here and ping if anything stalls. :thumbsup:
ingrid: First recent datapoint hit the console at 1729462900 — customer should see updated charts in a few minutes. Closing loop with Zendesk now.
sam: Closing here once Zendesk confirms. Thanks all!"
